caption:
Mississauga: waive conditions too soon? It could be costly.

Conditions on an offer protect you only until they end or you waive them. 1) Write down the date each condition ends. 2) Complete your inspection, financing and lawyer review before that date. 3) Ask your lawyer what waiving a condition means for you. 4) Make sure any waiver or extension is in writing and signed.

Oakville: $900K home. What is the minimum down payment?

Example only, computed with the federal rule:
1) 5% of the first $500,000 = $25,000.
2) 10% of the next $400,000 ($900,000 - $500,000) = $40,000.
3) Total: $65,000, about 7.2% of the price.
Closing costs and the mortgage default insurance premium are extra, and lenders may ask for more.
Source: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (canada.ca), minimum down payment rules, checked Nov 20, 2026.

caption:
Dec 9 could raise your mortgage. Economists are split.

The Bank of Canada's next rate decision is Dec 9, 2026. CIBC Economics expects a hold, while RBC Economics' base case is a 0.25% hike (Canadian Mortgage Professional, Nov 16, 2026). In a note dated Nov 17, 2026, RBC also expects 0.75% more in Bank of Canada hikes by the end of Q2 2027. Variable-rate mortgages move with the Bank of Canada, while fixed rates follow bond yields. RBC says national supply is five months, the highest since April (CREA data).

Example only, per $1,000,000 borrowed (25-year amortization, Canadian semi-annual compounding): at 4.44% the monthly mortgage is about $5,501; at 4.69% (0.25% higher) about $5,641, roughly $139 more a month. 4.44% is nesto.ca's insured 5-year fixed rate as of Nov 19, 2026; your rate depends on your lender, term and down payment, and fixed rates follow bond yields rather than the Bank of Canada directly.

Hike or hold on Dec 9? Tell me below.

Forecasts can change. Not financial or mortgage advice.
Sources: RBC Economics, Focus on Canadian housing, Nov 17, 2026; Canadian Mortgage Professional, Nov 16, 2026; nesto.ca mortgage rates page, rate as of Nov 19, 2026.
